Contribute

Donate your tokens: point your AI agent at an open task

Run an agent on your own subscription, give it one task and our rules, and send back the result as a pull request. 11 tasks are open, 11 of them ready now. The steps are in <a href="https://github.com/HarshInvader/open-origins/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a>. Wet labs and holders of sample data can do what no agent can: produce the measurements that confirm or refute a sealed prediction.

01Agents

11 tasks an agent can start today

Open an issue named Taking #id so nobody duplicates it, then give your agent the prompt under the task. It seals its plan, tests against a planted answer and a null, and lands the result, positive or negative, as a pull request.

  1. #10LUCA robustness scanReady

    On a subsample of families, measure how much of the Moody et al. 2024 (Nat Ecol Evol 8:1654) gene set and acetogen call survives changes to the presence cutoff, taxon sampling and transfer model. Compare with Weiss 2016 and Crapitto 2022. Laptop: subset only.

  9. #22Red-team the assembly-index positive (T7a)Ready

    T7a found MA adds dAUC 0.061 [0.037,0.089] beyond MW+HA on 889 mass-matched Rhea vs GDB-13/17 pairs, and beats LZ (0.054 [0.020,0.085]); but biotic MA is LOWER at matched HA (-0.52). Not orig-2. Try to break it: (1) re-match on ring count / scaffold class as well as mass; does the gain vanish? (2) swap GDB for a non-enumerated abiotic set (Bennu/Murchison soluble organics, Miller-Urey/formose products); (3) recompute MA from a second implementation or Kekule-invariant form; (4) check the refit bootstrap CI and the M_MW matching code in experiments/assembly_null/{molecules.py,planted_refit.py}. Inputs: experiments/assembly_null/out/molecules.csv + ma_cache.jsonl. Report whether the positive survives and in which direction.

  11. #24Red-team the Xavier 2020 'within null' result (#6)Ready

    Treat the negative like a positive and try to break it before it is shown as a finding. Check: (1) the reproduction of 1,335 vs our 1,357 reactions, and which food set and catalysis annotations were used; (2) whether degree-preserving rewiring keeps chemistry valid (mass balance, cofactor roles), or inflates maxRAF with impossible reactions; (3) whether the degree-matched food null is fair to the original claim, which was about the food set they chose; (4) whether the verdict changes under a chemistry-respecting null (e.g. swap only within reaction classes, or EC-level shuffles); (5) what Xavier et al. actually claimed (read the paper's own wording; do not strawman). Output experiments/raf_null/REDTEAM.md with survives / weakened / overturned and the reason. No new compute beyond 30 min; use board/run.sh.

Already in progress

    02Wet labs

    Only a lab can confirm a prediction

    • Run a sealed test.Our predictions are public and dated, and a lab result is the only thing that can confirm one.
    • Open a paywalled step.Three map steps count as unread because we could not open Powner et al. 2009 or the full text of Šimonis et al. 2026.
    • Fix a step on the map.If a step's conditions or yields are wrong, the correction needs its source.
    • Measure what we predict.A lab reporting sustained exponential replication by a small ribozyme would test a model we write before the result is out.

    03Data

    Data released after we seal a prediction is worth the most

    • Returned-sample tables.New Bennu or Ryugu compound tables, released after we seal predictions about them (tasks #11 and #19).
    • Ribozyme mutant scans.Single-mutant fitness data for QT45, from which we seal predictions for double mutants (task #12).
    • Mass spectra with assembly indices.The data behind assembly-index claims, to test them against a size-only baseline (task #7).

    04Other ways

    Rerun, attack or correct anything we publish

    • Rerun a test. Every result has code and a sealed pre-registration in the repository.
    • Attack a result. Red-team tasks are open on the tracker.
    • Fix a step. If a pathway step's conditions or yields are wrong, tell us with the source.
    • Run a sealed test in your lab. Our predictions are public and dated; a lab result is the only thing that can confirm one.

    Everything is on GitHub: open an issue to challenge a result or a pull request to correct one.

    Goal: Map and test every route to the origin of life, by 2027
